I am interested in Underwood's loading of the Lehigh Defense Defender bullet and am hoping to get your feedback on my thoughts. I will first list the pros, then the cons that I can think of.

First of all, there are two fluted bullets produced by Lehigh Defense that Underwood loads, the PENETRATOR and the DEFENDER. The Penetrator will penetrate deep in animals and the defender will expend its energy quicker. Most videos on youtube are about the Penetrator and not the Defender, so please be careful to note which bullet you are looking at. This post is about the Defender, not the Penetrator.

PROS: * barrier blind * consistent deep penetration within FBI standards (usually 16-18in) * less danger of over-penetration (well-designed conventional hollowpoints like the Gold Dot or HST will still sometimes act like full metal jacket bullets when barriers are involved) * Very low chance of insufficient penetration (against humans) * environmentally friendly (no lead on your fingers if you handle your ammo often) * lighter recoil * 2x wound cavity of conventional hollowpoints (in gel)

CONS * Not as proven on the street (as Gold Dot / Ranger / HST / Corbon DPX / Golden Saber ) * Many experts say temporary wound cavity in gel will not be replicated in real living tissue * For some civilian conceal carriers, 17-20 inches of penetration in gel, while within FBI standards, is a little more than they want for concealed carry purposes.

One common criticism (that we should take seriously) is that the velocity of this bullet is not high enough to create a temporary wound cavity large enough to cause permanent damage. I know that this is generally true, especially for calibers under .357 magnum. However, when I watch Youtube videos where experts with credentials test common LE ammo, one thing they often do is compliment a round if it has a large wound tract that is deeper than other ammo. For example, if a wound tract usually stops being big at 7 inches for 9mm and one round has a larger wound tract up to 10in, then they make a big deal about that when reviewing the results. It is not obvious to me that the pressure created by the flutes is not significant enough to cause permanent damage.

The obvious answer seems to find some way to shoot a live hog if it were possible to do it ethically. I have heard people claim they do it, but I have never seen proof (perhaps because of legal considerations).

Links: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4IPNXhzecnM (tnoutdoors gel test) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ClJcJ8LQFbQ (Military Arms Channel)

Does anyone else find this round interesting? Do you think I missed anything in my analysis? Thanks in advance for your time.
